newsitem.title: UK: Tarmac consortium wins UK motorway contract.
newsitem.headline: Tarmac consortium wins UK motorway contract.

text.p: Tarmac Plc said a consortium, in which it is a 20 percent shareholder, has won a motorway improvement, operations and maintenance contract from the UK government.

The consortium, UK Highways Plc, comprises Tarmac - 20 percent, John Laing Plc - 20 percent, Hyder Plc - 40 percent, France's Caisse des Depots et Consignations - 16 percent and Transroute International - four percent.
Initial construction work to upgrade and maintain the M40 motorway in the south west of England will amount to about 75 million stg.

Under the contract, which is part of the government's private finance initiative, UK Highways will improve, run and maintain 122 kilometres of the M40 motorway between London and Warwick in central England.
The government will pay the consortium in the form of traffic-related "shadow" tolls, over 30 years.
Total project finance for the contract of 100 million stg has been raised via equity and a limited resource loan facility of 90 million stg from Midland Bank Plc.
The work includes widening part the motorway between junctions 1A and 3 from three to four lanes, plus major maintenance work.

Tarmac Laing Joint Venture, a construction partnership, will design, build and commission the M40 upgrade and initial maintenance work. Hyder Consulting will be infrastructure designers for the project.
